title: Separate delivery and retry executors to reduce head-of-line blocking
creator: Aisha Mehra
description:
Background: Our current queue consumer topology funnels both initial delivery attempts and delayed/retry work through the same executor pool and admission path. Long-running retry backoffs (large delays, or retries that rehydrate large payloads) can occupy worker threads and cause head-of-line blocking for fresh arrivals, increasing P99 latency and triggering tenant-level backpressure cascades. This ticket splits responsibilities: a dedicated delivery executor for on-the-wire, low-latency delivery and a separate retry/delay executor optimized for batching, serialized retry timers, and lower priority resource usage.

Goals:
- Eliminate head-of-line blocking caused by retry work on delivery paths.
- Provide configurable per-tenant concurrency caps across both executors.
- Reduce token-draw variance during traffic spikes via smoother retry draining.
- Preserve exactly-once / idempotent semantics already relied on by downstream workers.

Scope: Prototype and ship the executor split for both Redis-streams and Kafka consumer adapters, update admission and metrics, and roll out on staging then prod with dark-traffic validation.
acceptance_criteria: New executor architecture deployed in staging for redis and kafka consumers
P99 delivery latency (fresh messages) reduced by >= 30% under synthetic retry storms
No regression in duplicate deliveries beyond existing baseline (<= 0.02% increase)
Per-tenant concurrency knobs exposed in config and respected by both executors
Can simulate a retry storm in prod-small cluster and validate graceful degradation metrics
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Separate executors: simpler to reason about latency but increases thread count and memory usage. We'll use bounded pools with adaptive thread recycling to limit footprint.

Retry executor will support journaling of retry timers vs in-memory only: journaling increases durability after restarts but complicates shutdown; we'll default to in-memory with optional durable mode for high-commit tenants.
Prefer cooperative backoff (token buckets + jitter) on retry executor rather than aggressive shed: reduces tail risk but requires careful capacity tuning.
Kafka consumer prefetch shrink: decrease max.poll.records for consumers assigned to high-retry topics to limit long blocking loops — tradeoff is throughput.
Avoid schema changes to message envelope. We'll extend headers/metadata where possible to indicate executor hints.
Security impact: no secrets exposure. No new external endpoints. KMS/HSM not affected.
implementation_plan: 1) Add config flags for two executor pools (delivery_pool_size, retry_pool_size) and per-tenant caps
2) Instrument current consumer path to emit executor occupancies and task duration histograms (baseline)
3) Implement routing switch that places immediate deliveries onto delivery pool and deferred/retry messages onto retry pool; keep same message acknowledgement semantics
4) Implement a low-priority FIFO queue for retries with exponential backoff timer wheel; allow optional batching for small retries to improve throughput
5) Update Redis and Kafka adapters to honor executor hints and test local integration
6) Add e2e harness that simulates a production-like retry storm and run in staging with dark traffic shadowing
7) Gradual rollout: start with non-critical tenant group -> prod-small -> 25% traffic -> full rollout. Monitor SLOs and rollback on regressions
8) Post-deploy: cleanup and deprecate legacy single-executor flags and document new defaults
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for executor selection logic and ack handling
Load tests: synthetic retry storms combining variable delay distributions and payload sizes
Chaos tests: worker restart during large retry queue drain; confirm no message loss
Integration: ensure idempotency hooks still applied when messages moved between executors
Canary in prod-small with traffic mirroring and metric comparisons against baseline
notes: Related research: kernel-optimizations team observed that long GC pauses amplify head-of-line blocking — try to tune GCs on java consumers before increasing pool sizes
We should avoid increasing global thread counts for small machines; implement dynamic pooling that scales up to a cap during retry bursts then scales down
Consider future work: priority queues across tenants and weight-based fair-sharing if split executors are insufficient
